* refactor!: remove root-level .js shims and lock single entrypoint

Remove the 27 backwards-compat root-level .js shim files that re-exported from dist/. Consumers now import named exports from the single package entrypoint. Add an exports map pointing at dist/browser-detection and drop *.js from the published files array so subpath imports are no longer shipped.

BREAKING CHANGE: root-level subpath imports (e.g. "@braintree/browser-detection/is-android") are removed. Import named exports from the package root instead: import { isAndroid } from "@braintree/browser-detection".

* test: remove root-shim publish-integrity test

This test enumerated root-level .js shims and asserted each was a named export on the dist bundle. With the shims removed, the test is obsolete. The public API surface remains guarded by TypeScript and the per-module unit tests.

* docs: update README and CHANGELOG for single entrypoint

Replace require()/subpath examples with named imports from the package root and document the breaking change in the UNRELEASED changelog section.

* build: enable esModuleInterop and lock commonjs module output

Prepare the compiler for ESM source syntax while keeping CommonJS emit so the package's main/require entry and the browserify --standalone bundle continue to work.

* refactor: convert detection modules to ESM named exports

Replace TypeScript's legacy export = / import = require syntax with standard ESM named export/import across all detection modules and the barrel. Rename the is-ie function from isIE to isIe to match its public export name. No public API or behavior change.

* test: convert unit tests to ESM named imports

Update all unit tests to import named exports and add a typed user-agents helper (Record<string, string>) so dynamic AGENTS[key] lookups type-check under the JSON default import.

* chore: drop obsolete no-var-requires eslint override for tests
